(P1, conf 100)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — `TopicUser.find_by(user_id:, topic_id:)` assumes a row exists; a user notified via mention/category-watch/PM invite with no topic_users row gets nil and `tu.notification_level` raises, whereas `TopicUser.change` handles the create-or-update case; the unsubscribe path adopted a different (narrower) row-ownership contract than the rest of the model. (P1, conf 75)

app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107-111 — the "unsubscribe" action is a step-down toggle (watching/tracking -> regular, regular -> muted) rather than an idempotent target state, so the same emailed link means different things per click and two clicks silently mute the topic; the sentinel meaning of "unsubscribe" depends on hidden prior state. (P1, conf 100)

config/routes.rb:440-441 — a state-mutating notification-level change is wired to a `get` route (and `skip_before_filter :check_xhr`), while the sibling mutations (`mute`, `unmute`, `notifications`) are `put`/`post`; link prefetchers/previewers and browser history revisits change subscription state without user intent. (P1, conf 75)

lib/email/message_builder.rb:107 — `result['List-Unsubscribe'] = "<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>"` still advertises only the global preferences URL while the body now advertises `%{unsubscribe_url}`; the header and body now disagree about what "unsubscribe" means for this message (FORMAT-DRIFT between two unsubscribe surfaces). (P2, conf 100)

config/locales/server.en.yml:1852-1855 — `unsubscribe_link` now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` unconditionally, so `add_unsubscribe_link: true` is no longer sufficient on its own: any builder/caller (spec at message_builder_spec.rb:171 had to be patched, plugins/digest/future mailers) that omits `unsubscribe_url` raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`; the contract of `add_unsubscribe_link` changed without the builder enforcing or defaulting the new required key. adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new template that uses triple-stash: `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (topic/unsubscribe.hbs) and the controller computes that string via `I18n.t(..., { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`, while the translation contains raw HTML (`{{title}}`). This creates a concrete, diff-grounded potential XSS/sanitization concern because the rendered output is explicitly unescaped and depends on `model.fancyTitle` being safe. However, the finding’s claims about server-side escaping in `app/models/topic.rb:264` and `updateFromJson` fallback behavior are not verifiable from this diff, so it can’t be confirmed as an actual defect based solely on the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:172 — the only test change in the diff is fixture plumbing (`unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`) added to keep the pre-existing "has the user preferences url in the body" test green after `unsubscribe_link` gained a `%{unsubscribe_url}` interpolation; no assertion anywhere checks that `builder.body` or `html_part` contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL, so the feature's core email-body behavior ships with zero verification and a regression that drops the link (e.g. reverting the locale string) passes the suite. adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new interpolation to the server locale `unsubscribe_link` (`%{unsubscribe_url}` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`) and plumbs `unsubscribe_url` into the email opts (`app/mailers/user_notifications.rb`) and into the spec fixture (`spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`). However, the only spec change shown is the added opt; there is no added/updated assertion in this diff that verifies the rendered email body/html actually includes the per-topic unsubscribe URL. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for newly added behavior, not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:174 — `expect(message_with_unsubscribe.header_args['List-Unsubscribe']).to be_present` is a false-confidence assertion for this feature: `lib/email/message_builder.rb:107` still emits `"<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>"`, so the List-Unsubscribe header never carries the per-topic URL, yet the spec (with the new `unsubscribe_url` opt in the fixture) reads as if it covers it; a reviewer relying on this test believes the header was updated when it was not. (P2, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: From the diff, the only unsubscribe-related change inside `lib/email/message_builder.rb` is in `html_part`, where `%{unsubscribe_link}` is filled using the updated `unsubscribe_link` i18n string (now requiring `unsubscribe_url`). The spec update adds `unsubscribe_url` to the fixture, which is consistent with satisfying that template interpolation. The finding’s core claim—`MessageBuilder` “still emits `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>`” in the `List-Unsubscribe` header and that the spec falsely implies coverage of a per-topic URL—is not verifiable from this diff because the header-generation code is not shown/changed here, and the spec assertion still only checks presence of the header, not its contents.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb:168 — the diff silently deletes coverage of `add_unsubscribe_link: true` without `unsubscribe_url`; after this change that combination raises `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument` from `body` (lib/email/message_builder.rb:90) and `html_part` (:67), and no test asserts either a safe default or the raise, so any future caller (digest, plugin) that sets `add_unsubscribe_link` alone breaks with no red test. (P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `config/locales/server.en.yml` `unsubscribe_link` to include a new required interpolation `%{unsubscribe_url}`. In `lib/email/message_builder.rb`, `html_part` still does `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` when `add_unsubscribe_link` is true, but `template_args` only includes `unsubscribe_url` if the caller passed it in `@opts` (no default is set). Therefore, `Email::MessageBuilder.new(..., add_unsubscribe_link: true)` without `unsubscribe_url` will raise `I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument`. The spec change at `spec/components/email/message_builder_spec.rb` updates the test to always pass `unsubscribe_url`, removing coverage of the previously-valid call pattern and masking this breaking behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:98 — new `unsubscribe` action (slug redirect, `TopicUser.find_by` toggle where `tu` is nil for a user who never visited the topic and `tu.notification_level` raises NoMethodError, tracking/watching->regular vs regular->muted branching, `perform_show_response`) has no controller spec in the diff and no `unsubscribe` reference in any spec in the repo; every branch of the user-facing endpoint the email link targets is unverified. (P1, conf 100)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` can return `nil` for users without an existing `topic_users` row. The next line dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`), which would raise `NoMethodError` and break the unsubscribe endpoint targeted by the new email link. This nil-handling issue is directly visible in the diff; the claim about repo-wide missing specs cannot be fully verified from the diff, but the nil dereference is a concrete defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:500 — `render :show` added inside `perform_show_response` also changes the existing `show` action's html branch (explicit template instead of implicit) and is exercised by no test in the diff; if `show`'s implicit render previously depended on action name for any format-specific template the change is unobserved. (advisory, P3, conf 50)

adjudication.rationale: The added `render :show` is inside `perform_show_response`’s `format.html` block. When `perform_show_response` is called from the `show` action, Rails’ implicit render would already render `show`, so this does not meaningfully “change the existing show action’s html branch” as claimed. The explicit render mainly affects other actions (notably the new `unsubscribe` action, which calls `perform_show_response`) by forcing the show template, which appears intentional. The warning about previously depending on implicit action-name rendering for other format-specific templates is speculative and not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/mailers/user_notifications.rb:295 — `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` is threaded into `email_opts` with no mailer spec asserting the delivered notification email body contains `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe`; the wiring between mailer and builder is the integration point of the feature and is untested end to end. Rebuttal gate: a spec/mailers/user_notifications_spec.rb example matching the unsubscribe URL in `mail.body`. (advisory, P2, conf 75)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url` into `email_opts` in `app/mailers/user_notifications.rb`, and the unsubscribe link text now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}` in `config/locales/server.en.yml`. This is a specific, feature-integration test gap introduced by the change, not a proven runtime defect.
